propositions.text: The claimant is a citizen of El Salvador alleging refugee and protection status under IRPA sections 96 and 97(1).
propositions.quote: The claimant, XXXXXXXXXXXXXXXXXXXXXXX, is a citizen of El Salvador. Ms. XXXXXXX is alleging that she is a "Convention refugee" and a "person in need of protection" under section 96 and subsection 97(1) of the Immigration and Refugee Protection Act (IRPA).

paragraphs.summary: The claimant from El Salvador alleges refugee and protection status under IRPA sections 96 and 97(1).

propositions.text: The claimant alleges she met her future husband at 14 and lived with him without parental permission.
propositions.quote: The claimant alleged that she met her future husband when she was 14 years old and that she went to live with him without her parents' permission.

paragraphs.summary: The claimant alleges she met her future husband at 14 and lived with him without parental permission.

propositions.text: The claimant alleges her husband started beating her the same year and she stayed due to lack of support.
propositions.quote: He started to beat her that same year. She stayed with him because she had no other support.

paragraphs.summary: The claimant alleges her husband started beating her the same year and she stayed due to lack of support.

propositions.text: The claimant states that in 2002 her Canadian citizen husband decided to come to Canada and she followed him.
propositions.quote: She stated that, in 2002, since her husband is a Canadian citizen, he decided to come here to live; she followed him.

paragraphs.summary: The claimant states that in 2002 her Canadian citizen husband decided to come to Canada and she followed him.

propositions.text: They stayed in Mexico for 1.5 years to save money for their trip.
propositions.quote: They stayed in Mexico for one and a half years in order to save up enough money to continue their trip.

paragraphs.summary: They stayed in Mexico for 1.5 years to save money for their trip.

propositions.text: Upon arriving in the US, claimant was detained in Arizona as a minor, then reunited with spouse in Los Angeles and lived in Boston where son was born.
propositions.quote: When she arrived in the United States, she was detained in Arizona because she was a minor. She then met up with her spouse again in Los Angeles. They then went to live in Boston, where her son was born on XXXXXXX, 2004.

propositions.text: They married in 2005 and then came to Canada.
propositions.quote: They were married on XXXXX, 2005, and then came to Canada.

paragraphs.summary: The claimant was detained in Arizona, reunited with spouse in LA, lived in Boston where son was born, married in 2005, then came to Canada.

propositions.text: They entered Canada in 2005 with temporary authorization as spouse of Canadian citizen.
propositions.quote: She entered on XXXXXXX, 2005, with a temporary authorization, since she was the spouse of a Canadian citizen.

paragraphs.summary: They entered Canada in 2005 with temporary authorization as spouse of Canadian citizen.

propositions.text: They lived with husband's mother; husband was often absent, used drugs, and abused her.
propositions.quote: They lived with her husband's mother, but her husband went out often, used drugs and abused her.

paragraphs.summary: They lived with husband's mother; husband was often absent, used drugs, and abused her.

propositions.text: Husband beat her badly, broke glass door with her head, beat her with electrical cable; she feared police and shelter.
propositions.quote: Another day, he beat her badly. She went to a CLSC. He broke a glass door with her head and beat her with an electrical cable. She stated that she did not call the police because she was afraid and that she did not go to the women's shelter because she was told that it was like a prison and she did not need care.

paragraphs.summary: Husband beat her badly, broke glass door with her head, beat her with electrical cable; she feared police and shelter.

propositions.text: In 2008, husband tried to beat her; she left without child, later found out he couldn't forbid her seeing child.
propositions.quote: In XXXXX 2008, her husband tried to beat her and she had to leave without her child. He then refused to let her see him. She finally ended up at a women's shelter with her child, and she found out that he did not have the right to forbid her from seeing her child.

paragraphs.summary: In 2008, husband tried to beat her; she left without child, later found out he couldn't forbid her seeing child.

propositions.text: She received a deportation letter but was unaware of her status and feared returning to El Salvador.
propositions.quote: She found out that she had received a deportation letter, but she did not know what her status was. She was afraid of returning to her country.

paragraphs.summary: She received a deportation letter but was unaware of her status and feared returning to El Salvador.

propositions.text: She claimed refugee protection in 2008, three years after arriving in Canada.
propositions.quote: She claimed refugee protection in XXXXX 2008-three years after she arrived in Canada.

paragraphs.summary: She claimed refugee protection in 2008, three years after arriving in Canada.

propositions.text: The panel finds the claimant is not a Convention refugee or person in need of protection.
propositions.quote: Having analyzed the documentary and testimonial evidence, the panel is of the opinion that the claimant is not a "Convention refugee" or a "person in need of protection".

paragraphs.summary: The panel finds the claimant is not a Convention refugee or person in need of protection.

propositions.text: The panel is satisfied as to the claimant's identity based on passport and birth certificate photocopies.
propositions.quote: Given the documents submitted as evidence,1 namely, the photocopies of her passport, which was valid from XXXXXX, 2005, to XXXXXX, 2010, and of her birth certificate, which is in her possession, the panel is satisfied as to the claimant's identity.

paragraphs.summary: The panel is satisfied as to the claimant's identity based on passport and birth certificate photocopies.

propositions.text: The claimant's testimony was not credible regarding her alleged fears if returned to El Salvador.
propositions.quote: The claimant's testimony was not credible regarding her alleged fears should she return to El Salvador.

paragraphs.summary: The claimant's testimony was not credible regarding her alleged fears if returned to El Salvador.

propositions.text: The claimant testified about meeting spouse in El Salvador, his Canadian citizenship, their living arrangements, and marriage.
propositions.quote: During her testimony, the claimant explained that she met her spouse, XXXXXXXXXXX XXXXXXXX, in El Salvador when he was there on vacation. He is a Canadian citizen but was born in El Salvador. He allegedly went to the United States with his parents when he was around two years old and came to Canada later. She started living with him when she was 14 and he was 26. Sometime around 2003, they decided to come to Canada. She allegedly followed him to Mexico. He allegedly left her there for her to cross the border while he supposedly waited for her in the United States. After arriving in that country, she met her spouse in Los Angeles and gave birth to their son in Boston on XXXXXXX, 2004. They were married on XXXXX, 2005, before coming to Canada.

paragraphs.summary: The claimant testified about meeting spouse in El Salvador, his Canadian citizenship, their living arrangements, and marriage.

propositions.text: The panel is surprised claimant stayed 14 months in US without claiming asylum; her explanations were vague.
propositions.quote: The panel is surprised that she stayed in the United States for 14 months, from XXXX 2004 to XXXXXXX 2005, without attempting to claim asylum. Her explanations on that topic are vague.

paragraphs.summary: The panel is surprised claimant stayed 14 months in US without claiming asylum; her explanations were vague.

propositions.text: Panel accepts claimant's explanation for not claiming asylum in US due to young age, abuse, and following Canadian spouse.
propositions.quote: Given the claimant's young age at the time and the possibility that she was abused, as she alleged, the panel accepts her explanations for not claiming asylum in the United States because she was following her spouse, who later became her husband, and because, since he is Canadian, she was considering coming to Canada, her husband's country of residence.

paragraphs.summary: Panel accepts claimant's explanation for not claiming asylum in US due to young age, abuse, and following Canadian spouse.

propositions.text: Panel questions why claimant waited three years to claim refugee protection in Canada.
propositions.quote: However, the panel wants to understand why the claimant waited three years to claim refugee protection in Canada.

propositions.text: Claimant entered Canada in 2005 with temporary permit as spouse of Canadian; spouse promised sponsorship but claimant did not check status due to abuse.
propositions.quote: In fact, she entered Canada on XXXXXXX, 2005, with a temporary permit because she is married to a Canadian. She explained that he told her that he would apply to sponsor her, but that having lived under the yoke of her violent ex-husband for many years, she did not check her status at the time.

propositions.text: Claimant alleges spouse became more violent after arrival in Canada, with drug use and abuse incidents.
propositions.quote: Her spouse supposedly became more violent after they arrived in Canada. Allegedly, he was often away, used drugs and hit her often.

propositions.text: Claimant alleges an incident of being shoved against door and hit, bleeding, and visiting CLSC without submitting documents.
propositions.quote: On one of these occasions, he allegedly shoved her hard against a door and hit her on the legs and in the face. She allegedly bled and went to see a doctor at the CLSC, but she did not submit any documents on this subject.

propositions.text: Claimant gave vague and contradictory testimony about dates and frequency of CLSC visits.
propositions.quote: The date of this incident is difficult to establish. She replied that it happened before she left the house, around XXXXXXX 2008. However, the claimant mentioned at one point that she went to the CLSC a number of times. Once again, the dates of the visits are vague. She stated that her first visit occurred during the same month she left the house and then stated that it was in XXXXXXX 2008. She later stated that it started around 2007.

paragraphs.summary: Panel questions why claimant waited three years to claim protection; claimant alleges abuse and gives vague, contradictory CLSC visit testimony.

propositions.text: Panel surprised by failure to submit CLSC evidence and contradictions about incidents.
propositions.quote: The failure to submit evidence to support the fact that she went to the CLSC, as well as the contradictions regarding the incidents that took place, surprises the panel.

paragraphs.summary: Panel surprised by failure to submit CLSC evidence and contradictions about incidents.

propositions.text: The panel is surprised by the alleged visits to the CLSC and doctor and the domestic violence allegations.
propositions.quote: The panel is surprised by the alleged visits to the CLSC and to the doctor and, consequently, by the allegations of domestic violence that she experienced.

propositions.text: The claimant was often confused in her answers and did not submit CLSC documents to prove interviews or treatment.
propositions.quote: she did not submit any documents from the CLSC to show that she had four or five interviews, as alleged, and received treatment.

propositions.text: The claimant provided no real explanation for lack of documents.
propositions.quote: she provided no real explanation for this.

propositions.text: The claimant has been in Quebec for three years and is assisted by several lawyers for divorce and refugee claim.
propositions.quote: She has, however, been in Quebec for three years and is being assisted by several lawyers, for, among other things, her divorce and her refugee protection claim.

paragraphs.summary: The panel finds the claimant's domestic violence allegations surprising, notes confusion and lack of CLSC documents, but notes she has legal assistance in Quebec for divorce and refugee claim.

propositions.text: Only after deportation order in 2008 did claimant take steps: leave husband, claim refugee protection, go to shelter, start divorce.
propositions.quote: it was only after the deportation order was issued on XXXXXXX, 2008, that the claimant took certain steps, including leaving her husband in XXXXXX 2008 and claiming refugee protection in XXXXXXX 2008. She went to a shelter for battered women on XXXXXXX, 2008, and started divorce proceedings on XXXXXXX, 2008.

propositions.text: Divorce finalized in 2010 due to increasing violence from spouse.
propositions.quote: Her divorce was finalized on XXXXX, 2010-all of that because her spouse had become increasingly violent.

paragraphs.summary: The panel notes claimant only took protective steps after 2008 deportation order, including divorce finalized in 2010 due to spouse's violence.

propositions.text: Panel considered documents submitted: Personal Information Form, motion to institute divorce, divorce decree, court order against spouse, removal order.
propositions.quote: In addition to her Personal Information Form, the claimant submitted four documents to corroborate these allegations: a motion to institute divorce proceedings, her divorce decree, a court order issued against her spouse, and her removal order.

propositions.text: Panel also considered Immigration Canada seized letter confirming claimant stayed at shelter with son in 2008.
propositions.quote: The panel also took into account a document seized by Immigration Canada when the refugee protection claim was made: a letter from the XXXXXXXXX XXXXXXX dated XXXXXXXX, 2008, which confirms that the claimant started staying at this shelter with her son on XXXXXXXX, 2008, and was still living there as of XXXXXXXX, 2008.

paragraphs.summary: The panel considered claimant's submitted documents including divorce papers and a letter confirming shelter stay with son in 2008.

propositions.text: Panel accepts claimant was a domestic violence victim despite no police call or medical documents.
propositions.quote: The panel accepts the claimant's allegations that she was a victim of domestic violence, even though she never called the police-she was scared-and even though she did not submit any medical documents on this subject;

propositions.text: Victims of domestic violence can have difficulties testifying and memory lapses.
propositions.quote: because victims of domestic violence can experience difficulties testifying and have memory lapses,

propositions.text: Claimant's youth and difficulties may explain problems organizing thoughts and gathering supporting documents.
propositions.quote: it is possible that the claimant, who is a young woman (born in 1987), would have some problems organizing her thoughts and gathering the documents required to support her testimony.

paragraphs.summary: The panel accepts claimant was a domestic violence victim despite no police or medical documents, noting victims' testimony difficulties and claimant's youth.

propositions.text: Panel finds claimant's delay in claiming refugee protection reasonable due to domestic violence and young age when meeting spouse.
propositions.quote: the panel considers the claimant's explanations regarding her delay in claiming refugee protection to be reasonable, given that she was a victim of domestic violence and that she was only 14 when she met this man who is 12 years her senior

propositions.text: Claimant endured living under spouse's control with little outside contact.
propositions.quote: she endured living under his control and had little contact outside of her home.

paragraphs.summary: The panel finds claimant's delay in refugee claim reasonable due to domestic violence and young age with controlling spouse.

propositions.text: Panel questions what claimant fears if returned to El Salvador given spouse lives in Canada and is Canadian.
propositions.quote: The panel wants to know what the claimant could fear should she return to El Salvador, since her spouse lives in Canada and is Canadian.

propositions.text: Claimant fears former spouse could return to El Salvador to beat or kill her due to Canadian passport and lack of protection there.
propositions.quote: The claimant stated that if she returned to El Salvador, her former spouse could return to El Salvador at any time to beat her or even kill her, as she alleged at the hearing, because he has a Canadian passport and because there is no protection there.

paragraphs.summary: The panel questions claimant's fear of return given spouse in Canada; claimant alleges spouse could return to harm her in El Salvador.

propositions.text: Claimant never explained why spouse would want to return to find her; spouse was on holidays when they met and had no fixed address.
propositions.quote: Also, the claimant never explained why her former spouse would want to return to El Salvador to find her. He was on holidays when she met him; he was XXXXXXX on a team, and they had no fixed address, as they both lived at different addresses, as stated at the hearing.

propositions.text: Spouse's entire family is in Canada except grandmother in El Salvador.
propositions.quote: The claimant also stated that her former spouse's entire family is in Canada. His grandmother is his only relative in El Salvador.

paragraphs.summary: The panel finds claimant did not explain spouse's motive to return; spouse's family is mostly in Canada except grandmother.

propositions.text: Spouse has little reason to return to El Salvador; no residence there and family mostly in Canada.
propositions.quote: Therefore, the claimant's former spouse has little reason to return to El Salvador. He obviously does not have a residence there, and all of his family is in Canada, except for his grandmother.

paragraphs.summary: The panel finds spouse has little reason to return to El Salvador given no residence and family in Canada.

propositions.text: Claimant is mother of child acknowledged by father, which could motivate finding spouse in El Salvador if she left with child.
propositions.quote: The claimant, however, is the mother of a child who has been acknowledged by the father, which could constitute a reason for trying to find his former spouse in El Salvador if she were to leave Canada with the child.

propositions.text: Father has applied for Canadian citizenship for son as son of a Canadian.
propositions.quote: However, the father has applied for Canadian citizenship for his son, since he is the son of a Canadian.

propositions.text: Child custody not stipulated in divorce documents; son has Canadian citizenship; panel thinks claimant unlikely to leave Canada with son.
propositions.quote: Given that the child's custody has not been stipulated in the divorce documents and that her son has Canadian citizenship, the panel is of the opinion that there is little chance that the claimant would leave the country with her son.

paragraphs.summary: The panel notes claimant's child acknowledged by father with Canadian citizenship and finds claimant unlikely to leave Canada with son.

propositions.text: Panel does not believe claimant's allegations that ex-spouse intends to threaten or kill her in El Salvador, especially as he lives in Montréal with another girlfriend.
propositions.quote: Consequently, the panel does not believe the claimant's allegations that her ex-spouse intends to go to El Salvador to threaten or to kill her, particularly since she stated that he is living in Montréal with another "girlfriend".

paragraphs.summary: The panel disbelieves claimant's claim that ex-spouse intends to harm her in El Salvador, noting he lives in Montréal with another girlfriend.

propositions.text: Panel concludes claimant is not credible about threats from former spouse in El Salvador.
propositions.quote: The panel concludes that the claimant is not credible regarding the alleged threats that she might experience in El Salvador from her former spouse, who lives in Canada.

paragraphs.summary: The panel concludes claimant is not credible about threats from former spouse in El Salvador.

propositions.text: Panel does not believe claimant would be threatened because of gender if returned to El Salvador.
propositions.quote: although the panel does not believe that the claimant would be threatened because of her gender should she return to El Salvador,

propositions.text: Panel considers claimant's young age, 8 years outside El Salvador, 5 years in Canada, and having a son in Canada as reasons she wants to remain in Canada.
propositions.quote: the panel does consider that, given the claimant's young age, the fact that she has spent eight years outside El Salvador, that she has already lived in Canada for five years, and that she has a son in Canada, the panel understands that she would want to improve her situation and remain in Canada.

propositions.text: Panel lacks jurisdiction to grant refugee protection on humanitarian and compassionate grounds.
propositions.quote: it does not have the jurisdiction to grant her refugee protection status on humanitarian and compassionate grounds.

paragraphs.summary: The panel finds no gender-based threat but understands claimant's wish to stay; lacks jurisdiction to grant protection on humanitarian grounds.

propositions.text: Panel concludes claimant did not show serious possibility of persecution as member of particular social group (women) if returned to El Salvador.
propositions.quote: the panel concludes that the claimant did not demonstrate that she faces a "serious possibility" of persecution under one of the Convention grounds, that is, as a member of a particular social group-women-should she return to El Salvador.

propositions.text: Claimant did not show on balance of probabilities that she would face danger of torture, risk to life, or cruel and unusual treatment if returned.
propositions.quote: She also did not demonstrate that, on a balance of probabilities, should she return to El Salvador, she would be personally subjected to a danger of torture or to a risk to her life or to a risk of cruel and unusual treatment or punishment.

paragraphs.summary: The panel concludes claimant failed to prove serious persecution or risk of torture or cruel treatment if returned to El Salvador.

propositions.text: Claimant's refugee protection claim is rejected.
propositions.quote: Consequently, her claim for refugee protection is rejected.

paragraphs.summary: The panel rejects claimant's refugee protection claim.
